Isochoric Process: The thermodynamic process in which the volume remains constant is called an isochoric process. In this process, the working substance is kept in a non expanding chamber. Since there is no change in volume, the work done in sucha process is zero. Therefore, from the first law of thermodynamics, we have or, dQ Thus, whole of the heat supplied is used to increase the internal energy of the system. iv. Isobaric Process: The thermodynamic process in which the pressure remains constant is called isobaric process. This system is carried out in an expanding chamber in which the pressure is kept constant. So, the temperature and the volume of the system change. The amount of heat dQ given to the working substance is partly used in increasing the temperature Of the working substance by dT and partly used in doing external work. v. Reversible Process: The process which can be retraced in the reverse order, so that it passes exactly through the same state as in the direct process is called reversible process. Example Of reversible process is an infinitesimally slow expansion and compression of an ideal gas at a constant pressures vi. Irreversible Process: The processes which cannot be retraced in the opposite order by reversing controlling factors are known as irreversible processes. Almost all processes in nature are irreversible process. Examples, rusting of iron, dissolving of soap in water, decay of matter,.etc•
